paragraphs: Here's what I love, friend. The people heard a hard word, that God's house was in ruins while they were busy with their own, and they obeyed the voice of the LORD (Haggai 1:12). They didn't argue, and they didn't make excuses. The text says they obeyed "because the LORD their God had sent him," so they heard God behind the prophet's words (Haggai 1:12).

Now look at what God says right after they obey: "I am with you" (Haggai 1:13). That's the whole message, and it's short! I think that's the sweetest part. Obeying God doesn't mean walking into a job alone, because the One who gives the word stays right there with you.

And then the LORD stirred their spirits, and they came and began the work (Haggai 1:14). The stirring came from Him, and the work was real, so both are in the passage. So when you know what God has asked of you, friend, start, even if the first step is small and the dough hasn't risen yet. He is with you. The story isn't over, because this was only the beginning of the work.
